page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb-v2 is a dedicated bare-metal server configured with an Intel Xeon E-2388G processor operating at a base frequency of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 8 physical cores and 16 execution threads, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core. Compute resources are entirely dedicated without hypervisor overhead, featuring hardware instruction support for AVX-512 with VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA extensions. Memory capacity is substantial, providing 128 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3000 MHz, which equates to an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio.

Integrated local storage consists of a bundled 3840 GB NVMe SSD, delivering high-capacity, low-latency disk access directly attached over PCIe. The system includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address and does not feature a dedicated GPU accelerator. In benchmark tests, the Xeon E-2388G demonstrates strong single-threaded processing capabilities, reaching a Geekbench single-core score of 2184.0 and achieving top-quartile performance in single-threaded compression and small-model language generation. PassMark memory testing places the system within the top ten percent at a 3390.33 score.

Performance tradeoffs stem from the processor's client-derived architecture and dual-channel memory topology. Uncached memory bandwidth results measure 36.93 GB/sec for sequential reads and 19.38 GB/sec for writes, both falling within the lower quartile. Multi-core compute performance remains midrange, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 23271.22 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10124.0. Consequently, performance is skewed toward high single-thread clock velocity and large memory capacity rather than parallel throughput.

Providing high resource density with dedicated physical access, this server configuration offers solid cost efficiency for workloads prioritizing dedicated RAM allocation and fast local disk over extreme multi-socket core counts. Recommended workloads include relational databases, memory-caching tiers such as Redis, build systems, web application serving, and backend services that require single-tenant isolation and low disk latency.

The platform features no discrete GPU. Benchmark results highlight strong single-core CPU throughput, verified by a Geekbench single-core score of 2184.0 and top-tier PassMark memory performance of 3390.33, alongside strong single-thread compression speeds.
